question.text: A debt AIF holds a corporate bond with coupon 9% paid semi-annually. The last coupon was 3 months ago. When reporting fair value of the bond to investors, the 'dirty price' includes:

answer.text: Only the present value of future coupons (clean price only)
The clean price PLUS accrued interest (since last coupon date to valuation date)
The face value plus the next coupon, ignoring time value
Only the sale price in the latest exchange trade

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Dirty price = clean price (PV of future cash flows) + accrued interest from last coupon to valuation date. For a 9% bond semi-annual, 3 months since last coupon means accrual = (9%/2) x (3/6) = 2.25% of par. This matters for NAV reporting and investor subscription/redemption pricing. **The Trap:** Clean price ignores accrued — fine for market quoting but wrong for NAV (investor would pay less than the fund is owed). Option C ignores present value. Option D ignores accrued between trades. **Cross-Exam Context:** X-B and XV teach dirty/clean mechanics; XIX-C applies it to AIF NAV where the daily accrual affects the incentive-fee high-water mark calculation. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Verify your fund accountant's system computes accrued on an ACT/ACT or 30/360 basis consistently. Investors who redeem mid-coupon-period under a clean-price NAV effectively leave accrued interest on the table for remaining unitholders.
